thread:
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Hey team — SF Enterprise signed (PO in, legal done). Goal: staged go-live with 2 pilot teams on 2026-04-12. Key constraints: SSO via Okta, data residency in eu-west-1, and we should reserve ~3k QPS equivalent for inference (they expect bursty traffic). Renewal conversation starts in 9 months — flagged high risk if launch slips >30 days.
Aisha Khan (CS): Thanks Marco. Can you confirm source of sample traffic and who owns infra approvals at their side? Need contact + SAML metadata.
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Contact is emma@sf-enterprise.com, PM Sam L. Sam asked for a short runbook and ETA for Dedicated capacity estimate. I'll DM SAML metadata now.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): Assigning owners: Tess -> provisioning and quota; Ben -> infra readiness + network review; Aisha -> onboarding plan & customer Qs.
Ben Ortiz (Support): On infra: we'll need VPC peering or PrivateLink design. Quick check — do they accept AWS managed prefixes? Also: are they okay with a staged quantized model (8-bit) for tail latency?
Aisha Khan (CS): Emma said they require production parity on quality; conservative on quantization. Let's assume full precision for initial launch, fallback to quantized variants if cost/lateness tradeoffs needed.
Marco Ruiz (Sales): They prefer no model paraphrasing changes. Also they want logs retained for 90 days, and audit trail for inference requests.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): Creating initial checklist: 1) SAML metadata + test user 2) VPC connectivity design + CIDR approval 3) Dedicated capacity estimate + pricing 4) Runbook draft for pilot teams 5) Data retention + audit config 6) Support escalation path. Assigning owners inline.
oncall-bot: Ticket RI-8219 created: dedicated-provisioning/sf-enterprise. Assignees: tess.lee, ben.ortiz.
Ben Ortiz (Support): I'll start a short network survey. Action: @Marco please get their AWS account IDs and preferred connectivity (peering vs PrivateLink).
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Sent AWS account IDs to Tess and Ben via DM. Also shared SAML XML in the email thread.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): Quick notes for provisioning: use region eu-west-1, reserved pool = 4 x A10g (estimate), fallback policy = auto-route to hosted with throttling if capacity exhausted, can we enable prefix caching for initial tokenshare?
Ben Ortiz (Support): A10g reserve makes sense. I'll validate with infra if we can carve that pool by 2026-04-05. Risk: if GPUs aren't available we need a fallback play.
Aisha Khan (CS): Onboarding plan (first pass): week 0 — SSO test & account creation; week 1 — pilot team 1 integration; week 2 — pilot team 2; week 3 — smoke + quality evals; week 4 — go/no-go decision. Need sample prompts and eval set from customer by 2026-04-01.
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Emma committed to providing eval set and two engineer contacts by Fri (2026-03-26).
Tess Lee (CS Ops): Flagging dependencies and owners in the ticket. Also adding a quick cost scenario: baseline (full precision) vs alt (mixed-precision + caching) — will attach numbers.
Ben Ortiz (Support): Adding a network playbook checklist to the ticket. Also setting a tentative outage window for the migration test: 2026-04-09 02:00–04:00 UTC.
Aisha Khan (CS): Renewal risk note: because contract term starts now and significant feature SLAs are tied to launch, if go-live slips >30 days we trigger a customer success risk review and potential commercial concession. Flagging for revenue ops.
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Understood — I will keep execs looped.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): Quick ask for CS/Support: can we get a brief one-pager of the rollback plan and a contact matrix? I can include in the runbook.
Ben Ortiz (Support): I will draft rollback + incident contacts. Will ping SRE for playbook links.
Aisha Khan (CS): OK — next steps summary: Marco -> confirm eval set + SAML (by 2026-03-26); Tess -> finish capacity estimate + runbook draft (by 2026-03-30); Ben -> network survey + rollback doc (by 2026-03-28); Aisha -> onboarding timeline + pilot checklist (by 2026-03-30).
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Sounds good. One more ask from the customer: can we include a short performance SLA for tail latency (95th P90 < 300ms)? They want it in the pilot acceptance criteria.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): We'll surface realistic 95th/median numbers in the capacity estimate — if we can't meet 300ms in full precision we'll propose latency tiers.
Aisha Khan (CS): I'll include the SLA options in the pilot acceptance criteria.
Marco Ruiz (Sales): Thanks all :thumbsup:. If anyone needs the email chain I posted it to the ticket.
Tess Lee (CS Ops): I'll update RI-8219 with owners and the initial checklist.
oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: weekly-checkin set for Tue 09:00 UTC starting 2026-03-30.
